title: Facilitated biosecurity planning in client dairy herds of one veterinary practice: an implementation study
abstract: Aim: to assess whether facilitated biosecurity planning visits by the herd's own vet can be delivered in routine practice and are followed by adoption of observed core measures. Methods: implementation study in consenting client dairy herds, January to June 2027, with unannounced observation of five measures at baseline and six months and a delivery fidelity record. Results and conclusions will be written after follow-up.
introduction: Biosecurity advice is often not followed on dairy farms, and farmer report overstates practice. A randomised trial showed that facilitated plans with a few farm-specific priorities raise observed adoption; whether a single practice can deliver them is unknown.
methods: Each herd received one planning visit agreeing three priorities and a follow-up call. A second vet observed five core measures unannounced at baseline and six months. Delivery, reach and vet time were recorded.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present reach, delivery fidelity, change in observed measures and vet time per herd.
discussion: The discussion will interpret adoption in light of delivery and reach and describe what the practice would need to sustain visits.
limitations: Few herds, no concurrent comparison, volunteer farms and short follow-up.
summary: StaRI-structured draft with results left empty.
